summary: This note is a short biographical entry on Ibn Abbad al-Rundi, a leading Sufi theologian of the 14th century. It states his full name and lifespan (1333–1390), his birthplace in Ronda, and his emigration to Morocco at an early age, attracted by its famous madrasahs. It notes he spent most of his life in several Moroccan cities and was buried in the Bab al-Futuh cemetery in Fes.
one_line: Biographical entry on Ibn Abbad al-Rundi, a 14th-century Sufi theologian born in Ronda who spent most of his life in Morocco.
key_facts: Ibn Abbad al-Rundi lived from 1333 to 1390.
His full name is given as Abu 'abd Allah Muhammad Ibn Abi Ishaq Ibrahim An-nafzi Al-himyari Ar-rundi.
He was one of the leading Sufi theologians of his time.
Ibn Abbad al-Rundi was born in Ronda.
He was attracted to Morocco by the famous madrasahs there.
He emigrated to Morocco at an early age.
Ibn Abbad al-Rundi spent most of his life in Morocco.
He lived in different Moroccan cities, including Salé, Marrakesh and Fes.
Ibn Abbad al-Rundi was buried in the Bab al-Futuh (south-eastern gate) cemetery in Fes.
